description: An 8-channel serial (shift-register style) LED driver — one unit drives 2 RGB LEDs.
how_to_use: SI (serial data), SCK (serial clock), RCK (storage/latch) are the minimum 3 pins the microcontroller drives — a bit-banged shift-register protocol, NOT the board's real SPI bus despite the 'SCK' name coincidence (deliberately not marked as a protocol leg here, to avoid falsely triggering this project's SPI-bus protection). QA-QH are the 8 parallel outputs (not interchangeable). SQH chains to the next unit's SI. OE (tie to GND if unused) and SCLR (tie to VCC if unused) are usually tied off.

plain.what: A chip that controls colour (RGB) LEDs using only a few Arduino pins.
plain.how: Like the 74HC595: your program sends it on/off values and it drives the LED colours.
